Q: Using a C++ union for uninitialized memory A:

FYI, a struct, class or union is a stencil on how a section of memory is laid out, or how it should be accessed. Has nothing to do with whether or not the memory is initialized. If you want to access memory that is not initialized, use std::array, std::vector or use a pointer type. Some compilers may initialize the memory in Debug mode.

Q: Is it possible to execute package wrapped into archive as module A:

After digging a bit deeper into this: Just write from server import app.

Explanation: When executing a python zipapp it adds the path to the app to python path. So you can import everything from it by name without problems. Relative imports don't work because python doesn't know about any parent package. If you're interested at how this importing works, there are great answers out there (e.g. here).

Suggestion: To prevent any naming conflicts I think it would be good practice to use a structure like

./
├── mypackage
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── server.py
└── __main__.py

And then write the import like from mypackage.server import app.

Q: google sheets SUMIF based on other sheet A:

try:

=QUERY(A2:C, "select year(Col1),sum(Col2),sum(Col3) 
              where Col1 is not null 
              group by year(Col1)
              label year(Col1)'year',sum(Col2)'sub',sum(Col3)'total'", )

or:

={"year","sub","total"; QUERY(QUERY(A2:C, 
 "select year(A),sum(B),sum(C) 
  where C is not null 
  group by year(A)"), 
  "offset 1", )}

Q: How to prevent the virtual keyboard from getting stuck to the text field in Jetpack Compose? A:

You can achieve this by applying a padding Modifier at the right spot.
Please try the following code:

BasicTextField(
    value = "",
    onValueChange = {},
    modifier = Modifier
        .fillMaxWidth()
        .padding(top = 300.dp, start = 8.dp, end = 8.dp),  // set BasicTextField padding
    decorationBox = { innerTextField ->
        Box(
            Modifier
                .padding(vertical = 8.dp)  // set Keyboard padding
                .fillMaxWidth()
                .height(56.dp)
                .border(
                    width = 2.dp,
                    color = Color.Black,
                    shape = RoundedCornerShape(20.dp)
                )
                .padding(horizontal = 12.dp),  // set Cursor padding
            contentAlignment = Alignment.CenterStart  // vertically center Cursor
        ) { innerTextField() }
    }
)

Q: How to force Kubernetes to listen to specific interface A:

k3s by default binds to first public system interface.
To overwrite this behavior you need to provide --node-ip=<listen-ip> parameter to the server process.

According to the k3s server command docs:

Options are documented on this page as CLI flags, but can also be passed as configuration file options.

By default this configuration file is located at /etc/rancher/k3s/config.yaml , edit it to add the node-ip option:

node-ip: 192.168.40.1

If you're using Systemd and want to, you can also override the k3s Systemd service. This can be done by editing the /etc/systemd/system/k3s.service , or by creating a Systemd service override file in /etc/systemd/system/k3s.service.d/ and editing the ExecStart block to include the --node-ip option:

ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/k3s \
    server --node-ip=192.168.40.1 \

and restart kubernetes by running

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart k3s.service

This way Kubernetes will listen only on 192.168.40.1 using interface assigned to this ip.
